__comment: TAP LONDON — Places data. All opening hours and prices verified June 2026. Always check official websites before visiting as details can change.

items.name: Tower of London
items.description: Nearly 1,000 years of royal history in one place — Crown Jewels, White Tower, Yeoman Warder tours, and the famous ravens. Allow at least 3 hours. Book online to save and skip queues.

items.name: Buckingham Palace
items.description: The King's official London residence. State Rooms open to visitors in summer only (July-September 2026). The exterior, Victoria Memorial and Changing of the Guard are free year-round.
items.openingHours: State Rooms: 9 Jul-27 Sep 2026. Exterior & guard: year-round
items.entryFee: Exterior free; State Rooms paid (summer only)

items.name: Big Ben & Elizabeth Tower
items.description: London's most iconic clock tower, officially called the Elizabeth Tower, rises above the Houses of Parliament. Best photographed from Westminster Bridge. Free to view from outside at any time.

items.name: London Eye
items.description: Europe's tallest cantilevered observation wheel — 30-minute rotation with sweeping views across Westminster, St Paul's and the skyline. Book timed entry online to avoid queues.
items.openingHours: Daily 11:00-18:00; extended hours in peak season
items.entryFee: Adult from £32 — book online for best price

items.name: Tower Bridge
items.description: Victorian masterpiece with iconic blue towers, glass-floor walkways 42 metres above the Thames, and a bridge lift exhibition. The exterior is free to walk across — the exhibition requires a ticket.

items.name: St Paul's Cathedral
items.description: Sir Christopher Wren's baroque masterpiece with a vast dome, Whispering Gallery, Golden Gallery with panoramic views, and crypt. Worship services are free; sightseeing requires a ticket.
items.openingHours: Mon-Sat 8:30-16:30 for sightseeing; open for worship daily

items.name: Trafalgar Square
items.description: London's civic heart — Nelson's Column, four bronze lions, fountains, and the National Gallery looking on. Free outdoor events, New Year's Eve celebrations, and perfect for people-watching.

items.name: Houses of Parliament
items.description: The Palace of Westminster — seat of UK government — is one of London's finest Gothic Revival buildings. Stunning from Westminster and Lambeth Bridges. Guided tours available on selected dates.
items.openingHours: Exterior always visible; tours on selected Sat and recess periods

items.name: National Gallery
items.description: Over 2,300 paintings from 1250-1900 including works by Van Gogh, Monet, Turner, Leonardo da Vinci and Rembrandt. One of the world's greatest art collections — and completely free.
items.entryFee: Free general admission; special exhibitions paid

items.name: British Museum
items.description: 8 million objects spanning 2 million years of human history under one roof — Rosetta Stone, Egyptian mummies, Elgin Marbles, and the spectacular Norman Foster Great Court. Completely free.
items.entryFee: Free general admission; some special exhibitions paid

items.name: Victoria and Albert Museum
items.description: The world's greatest museum of art and design — fashion, ceramics, sculpture, jewellery, photography, and architecture across 145 galleries. The café and garden are wonderful too.
items.entryFee: Free general admission; special exhibitions paid

items.name: Natural History Museum
items.description: Blue whale skeleton, dinosaur galleries, gemstone vault, earthquake simulator, and a stunning Romanesque building. One of London's finest free experiences — book timed entry online.
items.entryFee: Free general admission — book timed entry online

items.name: Tate Modern
items.description: World-class modern and contemporary art in a converted Bankside power station. Free collection displays across the Boiler House and new Blavatnik Building, with paid special exhibitions.

items.name: Royal Observatory Greenwich
items.description: Stand on the Prime Meridian (0° longitude), explore 500 years of timekeeping history, see the famous red time ball, and enjoy sweeping views over Canary Wharf and the Thames.

items.name: Kew Gardens
items.description: UNESCO World Heritage botanical gardens with over 50,000 plant species. Palm House, Treetop Walkway, Japanese Garden, and seasonal flower displays. A full-day escape from the city.
items.openingHours: Daily from 10:00; closing varies by season (16:30-20:00)

items.name: Hampton Court Palace
items.description: Henry VIII's magnificent Tudor palace with lavish State Apartments, famous hedge maze, formal gardens, Great Hall, and riverside setting. A perfect full-day trip from central London.
items.entryFee: Adult from £30; book online in advance

items.name: Windsor Castle
items.description: The oldest and largest occupied castle in the world — home to the British Royal Family for over 900 years. State Apartments, St George's Chapel, and a charming riverside town nearby.
items.openingHours: Daily 10:00-16:15; closed on some state occasions — check website

items.name: Hyde Park
items.description: One of London's eight Royal Parks — 350 acres of lawns, the Serpentine lake for boating and swimming, Speakers' Corner, Diana Memorial Fountain, and Rose Garden.

items.name: Regent's Park
items.description: Elegant Royal Park with the stunning Queen Mary's Rose Garden (12,000 roses), boating lake, Open Air Theatre in summer, and home to ZSL London Zoo on its northern edge.

items.name: Covent Garden
items.description: London's most lively piazza — world-class street performers, boutique shops, restaurants, the Apple Market for crafts, and the Royal Opera House. Free to explore, perfect any time of day.
items.openingHours: Area open all day; shops typically 10:00-20:00

items.name: Leadenhall Market
items.description: A stunning covered Victorian market built in 1881 with ornate green and cream paintwork, pubs, wine bars, and shops. Famous as a filming location for Harry Potter and Bridget Jones.
items.openingHours: Market open Mon-Fri; pubs and restaurants open daily

items.name: Kyoto Garden
items.description: A tranquil Japanese garden gifted to London by the city of Kyoto — koi ponds, stone lanterns, waterfalls, and Japanese maples. Peacocks roam freely. A remarkable hidden oasis.

items.name: Postman's Park
items.description: A quiet Victorian garden beside St Paul's containing the Watts Memorial — ceramic tiles commemorating ordinary Londoners who died saving others. Deeply moving and almost always uncrowded.

items.name: God's Own Junkyard
items.description: A neon wonderland created by the late Chris Bracey — a warehouse crammed with glowing signs, vintage neon art, and pop-culture relics. Unmissable for photographers and night-owl explorers.

items.name: Little Venice
items.description: Where Regent's Canal meets the Grand Union Canal — colourful narrowboats, weeping willows, waterside cafés, and a floating art gallery. A calm and photogenic escape from the city bustle.

items.name: Leake Street Graffiti Tunnel
items.description: A 300-metre legal graffiti tunnel beneath Waterloo station — constantly evolving street art from London's best artists. Walk through en route from Waterloo to the South Bank.

items.name: Columbia Road Flower Market
items.description: Sunday morning flower market beloved by Londoners — stalls overflowing with blooms, independent shops, bakeries, and cheerful market banter. Go early for best selection, late for bargains.
items.openingHours: Sunday only: 8:00-15:00 (arrive before 10:00 for best choice)

items.name: Bermondsey Street
items.description: One of London's most characterful streets — independent restaurants, fashion boutiques, the White Cube gallery, and an easy walk to Borough Market and Tower Bridge.
items.openingHours: Street open all day; businesses vary

items.name: Neal's Yard
items.description: A tiny, colourful courtyard hidden between Seven Dials and Covent Garden — independent cafés, Neal's Yard Remedies, juice bars, and flower boxes on every windowsill. Instagram favourite.

items.name: St Dunstan in the East
items.description: A bombed-out 17th-century church left as a ruin and transformed into a public garden — climbing plants cover Gothic arches and window frames, creating one of London's most atmospheric spaces.

items.name: Pergola and Hill Garden
items.description: A romantic Edwardian raised pergola draped in wisteria, roses and climbing plants at the edge of Hampstead Heath. One of London's most peaceful hidden gardens.

items.name: Millennium Bridge
items.description: London's only pedestrian-only Thames bridge — walk across for an iconic view of St Paul's Cathedral. Best photographed at golden hour or after dark when the dome is lit up beautifully.

items.name: Primrose Hill
items.description: The best free panoramic view of central London — on a clear day you can see 13 miles of skyline from Canary Wharf to Wembley. Magical at sunrise, golden hour, and after dark.

items.name: Sky Garden
items.description: London's highest public garden at 155 metres in the Walkie-Talkie building — stunning 360° views, landscaped gardens, two bars, and two restaurants. Book your FREE slot well in advance.
items.entryFee: Free — must book online in advance at skygarden.london

items.name: Southbank at Night
items.description: Walk the riverside from Westminster Bridge to Tower Bridge — passing the London Eye, Tate Modern, Millennium Bridge and Borough Market. London looks its best reflected in the Thames after dark.
items.openingHours: Open at all times — best after 20:00

items.name: Alexandra Palace
items.description: Victorian 'People's Palace' on a north London hill with sweeping views of the city skyline. Free to visit the park and terraces — the venue hosts concerts, markets, and events.
items.openingHours: Park open daily; venue hours vary by event
items.entryFee: Free to visit park and terraces

items.name: Greenwich Park Hill View
items.description: Stand on the hill below the Royal Observatory for one of London's finest views — maritime Greenwich, the Cutty Sark, the Thames, Canary Wharf towers, and the City skyline all in one frame.

items.name: Borough Market Archway
items.description: The Victorian railway arches framing Borough Market's entrance make for one of London's most atmospheric photos — especially early morning with mist or in the evening with warm lighting.
items.openingHours: Market Mon-Sat; best for photos early morning or evening

items.name: Science Museum
items.description: Explore actual Apollo spacecraft, Stephenson's Rocket, and interactive galleries on flight, medicine, and the future. The Wonderlab IMAX is paid. Everything else is completely free.
items.entryFee: Free general admission; IMAX and some galleries paid

items.name: Thames Path Walk
items.description: Walk the riverside path from Westminster to Tower Bridge — 2.5 miles of landmarks, bridges, public art, street food markets, and some of London's finest views. Completely free.

items.name: Changing of the Guard
items.description: The ceremonial changing of the King's Guard with military bands, marching soldiers, and full pageantry. Free to watch from outside the palace gates. Check the official schedule before visiting.
items.openingHours: Mon, Wed, Fri & Sun at 11:00 (subject to change — check royal.uk)

items.name: V&A Free Galleries
items.description: Fashion, jewellery, medieval art, photography, ceramics, and theatre design across 145 free galleries. The cast courts alone — full-size replicas of Trajan's Column and Michelangelo's David — are extraordinary.

items.name: Sky Garden Free View
items.description: One of London's best-kept secrets — a free rooftop garden with 360° city views from the 35th floor. Book your slot weeks in advance at skygarden.london as free tickets sell out fast.
items.entryFee: Free — book in advance at skygarden.london

items.name: Regent's Canal Walk
items.description: Walk the towpath from Little Venice to Camden Market — 3 miles past narrowboats, waterside cafés, London Zoo's penguin enclosure, and Regent's Park. One of London's finest free walks.
items.openingHours: Open at all times; best in daylight

items.name: Westminster Abbey
items.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Gothic abbey where British monarchs are crowned and buried. Poets' Corner and the Coronation Chair are highlights — allow 1.5-2 hours.
items.openingHours: Mon-Sat 9:30-15:30 (varies by day, check before visiting)

items.name: The Shard
items.description: Western Europe's tallest building, with an observation deck on floors 68-72 offering 360° views across London — best at sunset.
items.entryFee: Adult from £28 — book online in advance

items.name: Madame Tussauds London
items.description: World-famous wax museum with lifelike figures of celebrities, royals and historical icons — always popular with families and photo-hunters.

items.name: Shakespeare's Globe
items.description: A faithful reconstruction of Shakespeare's original open-air theatre on the Thames — watch a play or take a guided tour of the exhibition.

items.name: Churchill War Rooms
items.description: The underground bunker where Winston Churchill directed WWII — preserved exactly as it was left, with an excellent audio guide included.

items.name: Kensington Palace
items.description: Royal residence and birthplace of Queen Victoria, set within beautiful Kensington Gardens — state rooms and royal fashion exhibitions open to visitors.

items.name: The Monument to the Great Fire
items.description: A 202-foot column commemorating the Great Fire of 1666 — climb 311 steps for a rewarding City skyline view, far less crowded than The Shard.

items.name: Cutty Sark
items.description: A meticulously preserved 19th-century tea clipper ship in dry dock at Greenwich — walk beneath the hull and explore the decks.

items.name: National Portrait Gallery
items.description: Recently reopened after major renovation — a free collection of portraits spanning British history, from Tudor monarchs to modern icons.

items.name: Somerset House
items.description: A grand neoclassical courtyard on the Strand hosting art, fashion and design events — the fountains and ice rink (winter) make it a year-round destination.
items.entryFee: Free to enter courtyard, exhibitions vary

items.name: HMS Belfast
items.description: A WWII Royal Navy cruiser permanently moored on the Thames near Tower Bridge — explore nine decks including the engine room and gun turrets.

items.name: Imperial War Museum
items.description: A powerful, free museum covering conflicts from WWI to present day, including a moving Holocaust Galleries exhibition.

items.name: ZSL London Zoo
items.description: One of the world's oldest scientific zoos, set inside Regent's Park — over 750 species including tigers, gorillas and a walk-through penguin beach.

items.name: Design Museum
items.description: A sleek, free museum dedicated to contemporary design, fashion, architecture and technology — one of Kensington's most underrated stops.

items.name: Kensington Gardens
items.description: A calmer, more elegant sister to Hyde Park — home to Kensington Palace, the Italian Gardens, and the Diana Memorial Fountain and Playground.

items.name: St James's Park
items.description: The oldest Royal Park, with the best view towards Buckingham Palace across the lake — pelicans, flower beds and a genuinely romantic bridge crossing.

items.name: Green Park
items.description: A simple, unfussy Royal Park between Buckingham Palace and Piccadilly — deckchairs, mature trees and a quiet contrast to its grander neighbours.

items.name: Richmond Park
items.description: London's largest Royal Park — 2,500 acres roamed by wild deer, with the famous protected view of St Paul's from King Henry VIII's Mound.

items.name: Bushy Park
items.description: London's second-largest Royal Park, next to Hampton Court Palace — wild deer, avenues of chestnut trees and far fewer crowds than Richmond.

items.name: Holland Park
items.description: A quirky, well-kept hidden oasis near Notting Hill — home to the famous Kyoto Garden, roaming peacocks, and a great playground for families.

items.name: Parliament Hill, Hampstead Heath
items.description: Wild, hilly heathland with swimming ponds and one of the finest protected views of the London skyline — a proper escape from the city.

items.name: ArcelorMittal Orbit
items.description: A striking sculpture-tower in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park with a viewing platform and the world's longest tunnel slide — genuinely unique London skyline views.

items.name: Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
items.description: The transformed home of the 2012 Olympics — landscaped gardens, waterways, cycling routes and the iconic Orbit tower, all free to explore.

items.name: Tate Britain
items.description: The world's largest collection of British art from 1500 to present, including Turner's entire bequest. Quieter than Tate Modern and genuinely underrated — most visitors skip it.

items.name: V&A East Storehouse
items.description: Opened April 2026 — a new V&A site focused on craft and making, with free permanent galleries and no booking required.

items.name: The Courtauld Gallery
items.description: A smaller, significantly less crowded collection than the National Gallery — but it holds some of London's best Impressionist work, including Manet's A Bar at the Folies-Bergère.

items.name: Moco Museum London
items.description: Cutting-edge pop, street and digital art across three floors — icons like Andy Warhol and Damien Hirst alongside Banksy and Tracey Emin.

items.name: London Museum
items.description: The relaunched Museum of London at its new Smithfield site — tells the city's history from prehistoric times to today, with the famous gift shop for London-themed books.

items.name: Leighton House
items.description: The former home of Victorian artist Lord Leighton, celebrating its 100th year as a public museum in 2026 — famous for the golden-domed Arab Hall covered in Islamic tiles.

items.name: The Sherlock Holmes Museum
items.description: Located at the world-famous 221B Baker Street address — a Georgian townhouse lovingly recreated as Holmes and Watson's Victorian home, complete with memorabilia and gift shop.

items.name: The Foundling Museum
items.description: Tells the story of Britain's first home for abandoned children, established in 1739 — a moving, underrated collection including works by Hogarth and Handel connections.

items.name: The Old Operating Theatre Museum
items.description: One of Europe's oldest surviving operating theatres, dating from 1822 — a genuinely macabre and fascinating look at surgery before anaesthetics, hidden in a church garret.

items.name: Kenwood House
items.description: A grand former stately home on Hampstead Heath with free entry to see works by Rembrandt, Vermeer and Frans Hals — genuinely world-class art in a stunning setting.

items.name: Museum of Brands
items.description: The only museum of its kind in the world — 150 years of branding, packaging and advertising, a nostalgic trip through consumer culture history.

items.name: Madame Tussauds London
items.description: World-famous wax museum featuring lifelike figures of celebrities, royalty, and historical icons. Interactive photo opportunities throughout, plus a Marvel-themed 4D experience.
items.entryFee: Adult from £39 — book online to save

items.name: Royal Academy of Arts
items.description: Britain's oldest fine arts institution, founded in 1768, staging major touring exhibitions alongside its famous Summer Exhibition — the world's largest open submission art show.

items.name: London Transport Museum
items.description: A genuinely fun museum tracing 200 years of London's transport history, with vintage buses, tube trains and trams kids and adults can climb aboard. Free entry for under-18s.

items.name: Emirates Stadium Tour
items.description: Explore Arsenal’s home stadium on a behind-the-scenes tour and visit the club museum. Tour routes can change on event days.

items.name: Stamford Bridge Stadium Tour
items.description: Visit Chelsea FC’s stadium and museum, with tour access to areas such as the dressing rooms and players’ tunnel.

items.name: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium Tour
items.description: Go behind the scenes at Tottenham Hotspur’s stadium and explore the ground beyond a matchday visit.

items.name: Wembley Stadium Tour
items.description: Tour the national stadium beneath its landmark arch and see parts of the venue normally reserved for events.

items.name: Painted Hall
items.description: Step inside the richly painted hall at the Old Royal Naval College, one of Greenwich’s great historic interiors.

items.name: The Chimney Lift
items.description: Ride a glass lift inside a Battersea Power Station chimney to a viewpoint over the river and surrounding city. Previously known as Lift 109.

items.name: Royal Mews
items.description: See royal coaches, carriages and working stables at the Royal Mews beside Buckingham Palace. Check the seasonal opening schedule.
